thread:
anya: FYI saw a short peering flap between eu-west and us-central during the canary this morning. Observed ~120ms extra tail latency and a couple of failed metadata calls.
kevin: oh no. any customer-facing errors?
anya: No user errors, but proxy warmup failed for ~40 tenants; KV lookups timed out once. Mostly operator-visible. :warning:
maria: did it trigger fallback to resident region or did it overflow to nearest capacity?
anya: Overflowed to nearest capacity. We have policy: route->fallback->region-variant. But the problem was stale residency header on a few requests so they were treated as resident writes and got rejected.
sam: can you paste the logs snippet?
anya: sure:
```
2023-05-24T09:12:11Z proxy:e63 WARN lease-check timeout for tenant=acct-42 res=eu1 header=resident
2023-05-24T09:12:11Z proxy:e63 ERR prewarm failed: kv-get timeout (500ms)
```
liz: Hmm. Sounds like our prewarm path doesn't tolerate transient peering loss. We should consider a short-lived 'soft-fallback' mode: if KV lookups fail within Xs, treat as non-resident for routing and mark a quick recheck.
kevin: Agreed. Need to be careful with compliance — can't silently break residency for tenants with legal flags. Maybe add a consent check: if tenant has residency_enforced=true, then don't soft-fallback; otherwise allow.
maria: Also add a circuit-breaker metric so ops can see how often we soft-fallback. We don't want silent data residency violations.
anya: Proposal: implement soft-fallback with 2s window + tenant allowlist check. Implementation plan:
- proxy: on kv-get timeout (<3s) return hint 'unknown' instead of hard error
- router: if hint=='unknown' && residency_enforced==false -> route to nearest-capacity with header "x-fallback-reason:soft-kv"
- metrics: increment counter 'soft_fallback.reason=kv_timeout'
- audit: emit an event to audit-log-stream for any non-resident write
kevin: Looks good. Add a feature flag (config per-cluster) so we can roll it in canary. Also a config param for timeout.
sam: For tests, simulate peering drops in the chaos-suite and assert we don't change behavior for tenancy with residency_enforced true. Also validate that KV cache priming replays after restore.
liz: One more: if we soft-fallback, we should enqueue a background 'reassert' request to the resident region to attempt the write-as-resident when connectivity returns; that keeps correctness for idempotent ops.
maria: Perfect. Ops note: when enabled, we should alert on >1 soft-fallback/minute per 1k requests.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: feature-flag 'soft-fallback-kv' -> canary on eu-west at 2023-05-24T12:00Z
anya: Will follow up with a brief runbook entry (how to flip off, how to see audit events). Thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll draft the PR and include the per-tenant opt-out checks.
sam: I'll add chaos tests.
anya: Closing loop later with rollout notes.
